Inflation Reduction Act 45Z Clean Fuel Production Tax Credit and the European Union’s ReFuelEU SAF requirement of 2% in 2025 growing to 70% by 2050 (EASA 2025; IRS 2025). Future production of SAF will depend on multiple factors including competition for feedstock, the advancement of technology pathways, and policies. The International Air Transit Agency conducted a study to identify potential SAF production (IATA 2025b). The study assumed 2050 global biomass of 12,000 million tonnes (Mt) and that 35% of this would be available for bioenergy and biofuels. After accounting for other bioenergy and biofuels use of biomass, the study assumed 1,580 Mt would be available to produce approximately 300 Mt (99 billion gallons) of biomass-based SAF (IATA 2025b). The study also evaluated power-to-liquids (PtL) potential and estimated 2050 availability of 1,000 Mt of biogenic carbon dioxide could be available to produce about 200 Mt (66 billion gallons) of electric-based SAF (IATA 2025). SkyNRG’s SAF Market Outlook report estimates about 18 Mt (6 billion gallons) of production capacity by 2035 based on analysis of plant announcements and their likelihood of success (SkyNRG 2025). The study suggests other methods to scale by 2035 through increasing co- processing at petroleum refineries could add 2 Mt (700 million gallons) and conversion of renewable diesel plants could add 4 Mt (1.3 billion gallons).
